item.description:

Each writer was a resident, worker or student in Napa County. Writers submitted one or two unpublished stories in either prose or poetry format, with a limit of 60 words per story. A winning story connected all elements together, showing creativity and originality!
Submissions were accepted in English from adults or youth age 18 or younger, or in Spanish from youth age 18 or younger.
Yountville Arts, Napa County Libraries and Friends of the Yountville Library sponsor this event. September 26, 2026

Enjoy a magical evening of live, **traditional Irish and Roots-Americana music and Irish dance**, and a potluck to celebrate the Harvest Moon in Sebastopol, California on Saturday, Sept. 26 at 5pm.

item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.

item.title: Si Pudiera Quedarme / If I Could Stay — Sun Sep 27, 4:30 PM — Petaluma Historical Library and Museum
item.description:
Film Screening & Conversation with Award-Winning Filmmaker Theo Rigby and a Special Guest
What does it mean to fight for the right to stay home with your family?
Sunday, September 27, 4:30 -6:30 pm
Petaluma Historical Library & Museum
20 4th Street \(Corner of 4th & B Street\)
Suggested donation $5-$10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds.
Reserve Here
Join award-winning filmmaker Theo Rigby for a screening of Si Pudiera Quedarme / If I Could Stay, followed by a conversation with Rigby and a special guest.
Filmed over five years, Si Pudiera Quedarme is an intimate and moving portrait of Jeanette and Ingrid, two undocumented Latinx mothers who enter sanctuary in Bay Area churches rather than face deportation and separation from their families.
